findings.observation: The candidate’s crown is dominated by repeated steeply oriented, elongated foliage masses, with conspicuous upright stems emerging through them. Both leafy references show more irregular lateral spray development, including shelves on the left and interlocking, spreading masses on the right. The difference concerns branch-bearing foliage organization, not photographic realism.

The apex and much of the candidate’s outline are visible, but outer lateral foliage reaches and is clipped by the image edges. Complete crown proportions and perimeter irregularity cannot be established.

Visible ascending limbs support part of the reference architecture. Dense foliage obscures the candidate’s repeated subdivision and outer twig taper, which are especially explicit in the bare reference.
The exposed candidate trunk supports a gray, smooth, continuous bark reading without deep furrows or thick plates. Fine shallow surface markings remain unresolved at this viewing scale.

The candidate’s base widens but has a comparatively simple, even termination. The references show more irregular spreading root contact. This is a secondary refinement rather than the defining crown blocker.

coverage.explanation: The visible crown is tall, broad through its middle, and softly rounded toward the apex, within the references’ broad outline range. Clipped lateral extremities prevent a supported assessment of the complete outline.

An upright trunk, ascending limbs, and some outward lower branches are visible. The dense candidate foliage prevents assessment of the extensive repeated twig subdivision and progressive outer slenderness visible in the bare reference.

Gray coloration, broad smoothness, and absence of prominent plates or furrows match. The reference’s fine texture and subdued shallow markings cannot be resolved on the candidate’s whole-tree trunk; the complete core trait remains unverified.

Dark recesses provide depth, but the dominant repeated upright foliage plumes differ materially from the irregular lateral sprays and overlapping, spreading masses shared by the leafy references. Variation in shelf prominence does not account for this difference.

Both show numerous small elements and a fine, busy crown surface. Broadleaf shape is insufficiently resolved in the candidate and the inventory itself marks this interpretation uncertain; a full match cannot be established.
The candidate has basal widening, but its relatively even, simple foot lacks the references’ visible irregular spreading root flares. This is a secondary refinement.
Lower foliage spreads beyond the trunk and descends while leaving the base exposed. Clipped outer sprays prevent confirming their complete reach and downward terminal character.
Broad tonal changes are visible on the candidate trunk, but the scattered pale spots, irregular patches, and faint linear marks shown in the reference close-up cannot be assessed at this scale.
Lighter muted greens on exposed upper foliage and deeper greens in recesses support the reference color range. Exact color balance is acceptable variation.

A dominant exposed lower trunk dividing into ascending limbs is compatible with the range of frameworks in the leafy photographs. Exact fork arrangement and symmetry need not duplicate either specimen.
The densely leafy candidate matches a supplied foliage state. The separate bare photograph does not require a bare candidate or establish a transition between specimens.
